newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the European institutions would be closed on Thursday and Friday. He said they would be open to the public on Saturday May 10.

Spokesman Jean-Christophe Filori said Commissioner Hans van den Broek and German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel would go to Sarajevo on Thursday in a bid to increase the visibility of the EU's financial efforts in favour of reconstruction and the return of refugees to Bosnia. He said they would express the international community's concern about the Bosnian authorities non-application of the Dayton agreements and lack of cooperation on the return of refugees.

Spokesman Patrick Child briefed on Monday's ECOFIN Council. He said ministers would examine Spanish and Portuguese convergence plans, the annual excessive deficit review, the 1998 Community budget, the single market action plan and the state of play of the euro coins.

Child said there would be a round-table discussion on the practical aspects of the euro on May 15, with 200 particpants from all involved sectors invited. The conference will be broadcast live on a big screen at the Centre Borschette.

In answer to questions, Child said the Commission considered Britain's decision to allow the Bank of England greater independence in setting monetary policy was a positive move towards the EMU. He also said he agreed with Britain's Chancellor Gordon Brown that the move might be insufficient to meet EU Treaty requirements on central banks' independence ahead of joining EMU.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/393: Communication on the control of synthetic drugs.
- IP/97/394: Major Trans European Network corridor launched in Poland with largest-ever PHARE grant.
- Memo/97/49: Calendar of the Commissioners activities for the week of May 12-16.
- Conclusions of the EU-Mediterranean ministerial conference in Malta.
